test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 5 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In the human circulatory system, all veins carry blood towards the heart. What is the difference between the pulmonary vein and other veins?

options.text: the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood
The flow of blood in the pulmonary vein is accompanied by pressure
The pulmonary vein has a small lumen
there are no valves in the pulmonary vein

solution:
The correct answer is __**the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pulmonary vein is unique among veins because it carries **oxygenated blood** from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.
 
• Unlike other veins, which typically carry **deoxygenated blood** from the body back to the heart, the pulmonary vein is an exception.
 
• The pulmonary vein plays a crucial role in the **pulmonary circulation** cycle, which is responsible for oxygenating blood.
 
• This oxygenated blood is then pumped out to the rest of the body by the left ventricle, ensuring the supply of oxygen to all tissues and organs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Circulatory System:**

 
 
• The human circulatory system is a complex network of the heart, blood vessels, and blood that circulates throughout the body.
 
• Its primary function is to deliver oxygen and nutrients to cells and tissues and to remove waste products.
 
• The circulatory system is divided into two main parts: the systemic circulation and the pulmonary circulation.
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary Circulation:**
 
 
• It refers to the movement of blood from the heart to the lungs and back to the heart.
 
• Deoxygenated blood is pumped from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs via the pulmonary artery.
 
• In the lungs, carbon dioxide is exchanged for oxygen, and the now oxygenated blood is returned to the left atrium of the heart via the pulmonary veins.
 
 
 
• **Systemic Circulation:**
 
 
• This part of the circulatory system carries oxygenated blood from the left side of the heart to the rest of the body.
 
• After the tissues have used the oxygen, the deoxygenated blood returns to the right side of the heart via the veins.
 
 
 
• **Heart Chambers:**
 
 
• The heart has four chambers: two atria (upper chambers) and two ventricles (lower chambers).
 
• The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and pumps it into the right ventricle, which then sends it to the lungs.
 
• The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the left ventricle, which then sends it out to the body.
